fields.Q1:
WHAT IS STANDING AROUND THIS ROOM MADE OF?**

On three of the four sides — nothing. There is no material to put a hand on.

On the north side only, there is one thing: a thin horizontal strip of **coursed stone or brick blockwork, two courses tall**, roughly 32×16px blocks in a running bond, warm brown-grey. That strip occupies `y≈198–230` and runs `x≈25–350` and `x≈437–710`. The same two-course strip is reused as a stub inside the room at `x≈140–250, y≈450–470`.

Everything below that strip (`y≈230–262`), and the entire west (`x≈55`), east (`x≈690`) and south (`y≈770`) boundaries, is not a material at all.
fields.Q1_WHY:
At 6× zoom / 9× brightness on `(160–345, 193–235)` and `(440–700, 193–235)` I can resolve two rows of rectangles separated by vertical dark joints, with diagonal hatch strokes across some block faces — that is blockwork. But scanning across the west edge at `y=400`: `x=54 (5,6,10)` → `x=55–56 (2,2,3)` → `x=57 (3,3,5)` → `x=65 (8,8,11)`. That is a two-pixel black seam and a ramp. There is no face, no course, no joint, no thickness. Same at the south edge at `x=300` and the east edge at `y=400`.

---
fields.Q2:
SOLID MASS, OR FLAT PATTERN AROUND THE EDGE?**

**A change of colour.** Not a pattern either — on most of the perimeter there is not even a pattern, just a value step.

What decided it: I ran a column scan down `x=355–370`, which falls in a gap in the block strip. From `y=190` to `y=261` the values climb smoothly and monotonically — `(6,7,10) → (8,8,11) → (13,12,15) → (16,14,15) → (19,17,16) → (23,20,19)` — with **no discontinuity at `y=198`** (where the block strip begins elsewhere) and **no discontinuity at `y=230`** (where the strip ends). Then at `y=264` it flips warm, `(20,15,11)` — the ground.

So the "outside darkness" and the band that reads as the top of the wall are literally the same fill, differing only by how far they are from the torch. There is one surface from the top of the screen to the edge of the ground, with a thin painted strip of blockwork floating on it. Nothing has thickness.

---
fields.Q3:
WHERE EXACTLY DOES THE GROUND STOP?**

Four different places, all abrupt:

- **North**, at `x=300`: `y=261 (16,15,15)` neutral → `y=262 (13,10,8)` warm. **One pixel.** The transition is a hue flip, not a value step — the ground is warmer than what's above it but *darker*. No bevel, no contact shadow, no lip.
- **West**, at `y=400`: `x=55–56` two-pixel black seam `(2,2,3)`, then a ~8px ramp to `(8,8,11)` at `x=65`. ~10px total.
- **South**, at `x=300`: `y=761 (10,9,11)` fading down to `y=773 (2,2,2)` over 12px, then a one-pixel jump up to `(6,6,10)` at `y=774`. ~13px total.
- **East**, at `y=400`: `x≈690 (7,7,8)` → `x=700 (4,4,5)` → `x=720 (6,6,8)`. ~10px.

The west/south/east transitions are consistent with each other. The north transition is a different animal entirely — a hue change with no seam.

---
fields.Q4:
WHAT IS HOLDING THIS PLACE TOGETHER?**

**NOTHING.** There is nothing visible in this image holding anything up.

I went looking specifically. At 6× on the full north strip `(20–710, 193–266)` I can find: block joints, diagonal hatch scratches, dark diagonal lines. The dark diagonals are not braces — I traced one at `(500–700, 120–290)` and it runs continuously from the void at `y≈130`, through the block strip, across the blank band, and into the ground, at identical weight and colour the whole way. It is an overlay drawn across everything including empty space. It is not attached to anything.

No rope, no driven pin, no timber baulk, no strap, no shoring, no wedge, no plate. For a place held by a company that has been repairing it for four hundred years, there is not one repair on it.

---
fields.Q5:
BUILT, OR AN IMAGE THAT WAS REPEATED?**

**Built** — narrowly, and only where there is anything at all.

I ran a self-correlation on the block strip (`y=200–230, x=60–700`), high-passed to strip out the lighting gradient. Best correlation across all offsets from 8 to 320px was **r=0.105** at offset 244. That is noise. Nothing repeats at a fixed pitch; the block courses are varied cell to cell. That is authored, not stamped.

But the strip is the only thing that qualifies. The rest of the perimeter isn't repeated either — it just isn't there.

---
fields.Q6:
WOULD YOU BELIEVE THIS SHIPPED IN A COMMERCIAL GAME?**

**YES.** Plenty of shipped mobile roguelikes bound their rooms exactly this way.

Merely competent, or genuinely good? **Merely competent, and the standing structure specifically is below that.** The lighting falloff is handled well and the figure reads cleanly. But the subject I was asked about — the walls — is a thin decal on three sides of absence. A wall that is the same pixels as the void it separates you from is not a wall.

---
fields.Q7:
AT 1:1, WHAT CAN YOU ACTUALLY SEE ON THE STANDING SURFACES?**

**Legible at 1:1:** nothing. Not "a little" — nothing. The north structure at 1:1 is a horizontal dark bar, marginally less black than the space above it, and I can see *that it is there*. I cannot see what it is made of. I cannot see a single block, a single joint, or a single course line.

The wall stub at `(140–250, 450–510)` is the one exception: at 1:1 I can see a dark rectangle with a lighter grey patch beside it. I can see a shape. I still cannot see a material.

**Only on magnification:** the two courses; the block joints; the running bond; the diagonal hatch strokes; the pale lilac blobs; the crack overlay.

**Does it change with distance from the figure?** No, and that is the problem. The torch sits at `≈(400,485)`. The nearest standing structure — the north strip — is `≈270px` away, well outside the useful light radius. The wall stub at `x≈200, y≈460` is only ~200px away and is the brightest piece of structure in the frame, and it still resolves to a grey rectangle. **There is no distance at which the wall material becomes legible, because there is no wall inside the lit radius at all.** The light and the structure never meet.

I measured the ceiling: peak channel-sum across the entire north strip `(20–715, 193–236)` is **72 out of 765** — about 24 per channel. The material tops out at 9% of white.
fields.Q7_WHY:
- Checked at **1:1** (from the full 750×909 render): north strip `x 25–710, y 195–262`; corridor mouth `x 375–437, y 190–262`; wall stub `x 140–250, y 440–510`; west boundary `x 40–70, y 300–700`; south boundary `x 60–690, y 750–790`.
- Had to **magnify** (4–10×, brightness 3–11×) before anything appeared: `(160–345, 193–235)` at 6×/9× for the courses; `(440–700, 193–235)` at 6×/9×; `(395–450, 193–240)` at 10×/7× for the crack and blob; `(140–250, 440–510)` at 6×/4× for the stub; `(500–700, 120–290)` at 4×/6× for the crack crossing.
- Texture residual after removing the lighting gradient (Gaussian σ=9 high-pass, 0–255 scale): block strip `y200–228` **std 1.99**; blank band `y232–260` **std 1.64**; pure void `y100–128` **std 0.33**. At displayed values of 10–20, a std of 1.6–2.0 is below the visible threshold on a phone.

---
fields.Q8:
IS THERE ANYTHING YOUR EYE KEEPS RETURNING TO?**

Yes. **Pale lilac-grey blobs on the north strip.** Irregular lumps, roughly 10–14px across, in a desaturated violet that is cooler and lighter than anything else on the structure.

I detected **17 of them** along `y=196–230`, at `x ≈ 36, 93, 157, 188, 189, 252, 290, 294, 327, 372, 439, 496, 517, 538, 561, 615, 686` — roughly one every 40px, confined to two rows. I put two of them side by side (`(303–333, 199–221)` and `(536–566, 204–226)`): not pixel-identical, but unmistakably the same motif, same colour family, same size.

They are the only chromatic note on the structure besides the torch warmth, and the brightest thing on it. Which produces a bad result: magnified, the wall reads as *speckled* rather than as masonry — the blobs out-compete the courses for attention. At 1:1 they are invisible, so they buy nothing. They cost legibility at the only scale where the wall is examined and deliver nothing at the scale it is played.

---
fields.Q9:
WHAT IS BEYOND THE WALLS?**

**It is the same undifferentiated fill that the wall itself is made of.** That is the finding.

At 6× brightness over `(0–750, 0–200)` the void resolves as a soft blue-purple field of large organic blobs — a blurred noise layer — with thin dark meandering lines running through it. It is not more stone, not empty space, not another room. It is a fog overlay.

Two things told me it is the same surface as the "wall":
1. The column scan at `x=355–370` (through the gap in the block strip) runs continuously from void to ground with no material boundary at `y=230`.
2. In the 8× full-width view of `(20–710, 193–266)`, the large soft cloud blobs that fill the void **continue into the band below the block strip**, same scale, same shape language, unbroken.

And the crack lines run across the void as freely as across the ground — visible descending through `(500–700, 120–290)` and again below the south boundary at `(30–260, 720–830)`, where a vein continues past `y=774` into territory where there is no surface for a crack to be in. Cracks in nothing.

---
fields.Q10:
COULD YOU TELL A WAY THROUGH FROM A DEAD END WITHOUT WALKING INTO IT?**

Found it — a ~62px opening at `x≈375–437` running north from `y≈262` up to `y≈40`.

**At the mouth: a passage.** The one cue is hue. At `y=245`, inside the gap `x=384–432` reads `(35,27,21)` — warm, ground-coloured — while at the same row `x=300` reads `(14,13,14)`, neutral. Ground material continues through the opening. That works.

**Above `y≈230`: ambiguous.** It degrades to a dark vertical bar. The tile grid is still in there — I confirmed it at 4×/5× on `(330–480, 40–290)`, the courses run all the way to `y≈40` — but at 1:1 it is a black rectangle. You would guess, not read.

**And there is a false opening.** At `y=212`, `x=345–372` reads `(11,10,13)` — blue-dominant, the exact signature of the void, not the warm block colour. The left block run stops one full cell short of the corridor's west edge. At 1:1 that makes the opening look ~90px wide instead of 62px, or reads as a second blocked doorway right beside the real one. A player would try to walk into it.

---
fields.Q11:
HAS ANYTHING HAPPENED TO THIS STRUCTURE?**

Nothing has happened to it, and nothing has been done to it.

What I read that from: the only marks on the block strip are the diagonal crack lines, and those are not damage to *this* structure — they are a global overlay drawn at identical weight over the blockwork, over the blank band, over the ground, and over empty void. A crack layer that ignores what it is cracking is not a record of anything happening. There is no spalled block, no course sagging out of line, no gap packed with anything, no soot, no water staining, no chipped arris, no block replaced with a different one. The lilac blobs might be intended as mould, but they sit *on top* of undamaged blockwork rather than in it, and they scatter evenly rather than pooling where water would go.

This is a wall in as-built condition with a decal of cracks laid over it. For a place in continuous heavy use since before records, held by a company that has been repairing it for four centuries, its condition is: new, and never touched.

---
fields.Q12:
THE DARKER BAND — WALL TOP, OR MORE GROUND?**

**CANNOT TELL — and that is a defect, not an observation.** It is not distinguishable as either, because it is the same pixels as the void.

What decided it: through the gap at `x=355–370` the band is continuous with the darkness above it, one unbroken lighting ramp, no material boundary. And its residual texture after removing the lighting is **std 1.64** against **0.33** for pure void and **4.56** for a textured reference band — so it carries almost nothing of its own, and most of that little is the crack overlay passing through.

If forced to pick, I would say **wall top** on hue evidence alone: at `(300,250)` it reads `(16,14,16)` with blue ≥ red, while ground at `(300,266)` reads `(18,14,12)`, clearly warm. Ground does not change hue when it dims. But that is a spectrometer's answer, not an eye's.

Two things make it read wrong even so. It is **brighter than the first row of ground below it** — `(16,15,15)` at `y=261` versus `(13,10,8)` at `y=262` — which is backwards for a surface further from the light. And it is **32px, exactly one grid cell**, which is a wall's depth but reads as a strip of floor.

**One continuous surface, or squares?** **One continuous surface.** I scanned `y=245` across from `x=56` to `x=750` at 4px steps. From `x=140` to `x=372` the values rise smoothly `4 → 18` and from `x=440` to `x=600` fall smoothly `21 → 4`. **Zero cell breaks, zero seams, zero joints across roughly 550 pixels.** The only discontinuities in the entire scan are the corridor mouth at `x=376–436` and the map edges. Whatever this band is, it is a single flat fill with a radial gradient painted on it.

---
fields.CULL: Three of four sides have no wall at all; the north wall's inner half is void fill.
fields.FLIP LIST:
- Give the west, east and south boundaries the same two-course blockwork strip the north edge has, so the room is bounded by structure on all four sides rather than by a two-pixel seam at `x=55`, `x=690` and `y=770`.
- Give the 32px band at `y=230–262` its own top surface — cell divisions on the 32px grid and a per-cell value break of at least 6–8 units — so it stops being pixel-continuous with the void through the gap at `x=355–370`.
- Raise the block strip's internal contrast so the courses are legible at 1:1: it currently peaks at 24/255 with a texture residual of 1.99, and needs joint contrast around 5–8 units at that black level to register at all.
- Close the one-cell hole in the block course at `x=345–373, y=198–230`, which currently reads as a second opening beside the real passage at `x=375–437`.
- Put actual repairs on the blockwork — driven pins, lashed timber, packed gaps — and clip the crack overlay to solid surfaces so it stops running through empty void below `y=774` and above `y=198`.

---

The through-line: every defect here is one defect. The wall and the dark beyond it are the same fill, so nothing you did to the wall could ever be seen, and nothing that separates the player from the dark actually separates them. Fix the boundary first — give it a surface of its own — and the contrast, the damage and the repairs all become things that can exist. Right now there is nowhere to put them.

*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*

And it is **32px, exactly one grid cell**, which is a wall's depth but reads as a strip of floor.

**One continuous surface, or squares?** **One continuous surface.** I scanned `y=245` across from `x=56` to `x=750` at 4px steps. From `x=140` to `x=372` the values rise smoothly `4 → 18` and from `x=440` to `x=600` fall smoothly `21 → 4`. **Zero cell breaks, zero seams, zero joints across roughly 550 pixels.** The only discontinuities in the entire scan are the corridor mouth at `x=376–436` and the map edges. Whatever this band is, it is a single flat fill with a radial gradient painted on it.

---

**CULL:** Three of four sides have no wall at all; the north wall's inner half is void fill.

**FLIP LIST**
- Give the west, east and south boundaries the same two-course blockwork strip the north edge has, so the room is bounded by structure on all four sides rather than by a two-pixel seam at `x=55`, `x=690` and `y=770`.
- Give the 32px band at `y=230–262` its own top surface — cell divisions on the 32px grid and a per-cell value break of at least 6–8 units — so it stops being pixel-continuous with the void through the gap at `x=355–370`.
- Raise the block strip's internal contrast so the courses are legible at 1:1: it currently peaks at 24/255 with a texture residual of 1.99, and needs joint contrast around 5–8 units at that black level to register at all.
- Close the one-cell hole in the block course at `x=345–373, y=198–230`, which currently reads as a second opening beside the real passage at `x=375–437`.
- Put actual repairs on the blockwork — driven pins, lashed timber, packed gaps — and clip the crack overlay to solid surfaces so it stops running through empty void below `y=774` and above `y=198`.

---

The through-line: every defect here is one defect. The wall and the dark beyond it are the same fill, so nothing you did to the wall could ever be seen, and nothing that separates the player from the dark actually separates them. Fix the boundary first — give it a surface of its own — and the contrast, the damage and the repairs all become things that can exist. Right now there is nowhere to put them.

*Model: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)*
